column1: # HTTP response headers the http detector reasons about.
#   security   a hardening header - its ABSENCE from a response is the finding
#   disclosure the header leaks version/stack info - its PRESENCE is the finding
#   dangerous  the header value can itself be a problem (checked in code)
# severity is what a missing security header (or a present disclosure header) scores.

column4: HSTS. Without it, a browser can be downgraded to plain HTTP and the session stripped (sslstrip).
CSP. Without it there is no defence-in-depth against injected scripts (XSS).
Anti-clickjacking. Without it (and without a frame-ancestors CSP) the page can be framed and clickjacked.
Set to nosniff to stop MIME sniffing. Its absence enables some content-type confusion attacks.
Controls how much of the URL leaks in the Referer header to other sites.
Restricts powerful browser features (camera, geolocation, ...). Absence is a hardening gap, not a hole.
Advertises the server software and often its exact version - free version-matching for an attacker (and for this tool).
Advertises the app stack (e.g. PHP and its version). Pure information disclosure; turn it off.
Names the CMS/generator (Drupal, etc.), which maps straight to a version and its CVEs.
